title: hardening: under the protected profile the accounts CLI started from an IDE Accounts tab finds `claude` through the terminal's PATH, and on Windows claude.cmd finds `node` in the project cwd, so a project copy can run during sign-in
description:
Filed by architect-24611a0a on 2026-11-03 while planning task-26d9dc26bf334126bfb0bb4e9ed421aa. That task pins only the interpreter that starts the accounts CLI. Once the CLI is running, packages/moe-daemon/src/accounts/claudeAuth.ts resolves `claude` itself: MOE_CLAUDE_BIN, else `claude` on PATH.

- Windows: findWindowsCommand walks the PATH entries times PATHEXT. A '.' or relative entry resolves against the cwd, which is the project. A claude.cmd then runs through cmd.exe, and the npm shim inside it finds `node` in the current directory first unless NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath is set. That is the task-2f22237b vector, already fixed for the wrappers.
- POSIX: spawnSync uses execvp over the terminal's unfiltered PATH. The claude npm shim's `#!/usr/bin/env node` uses the same PATH.
- WSL agent mode is already covered: task-26d9dc26's in-WSL PATH filter is inherited by node and claude.
- `claude auth login` also runs with cwd = the project, so decide whether a protected Accounts terminal should open outside the project, for example in the user's home, so the project's .claude settings are never read during sign-in.

Possible shapes:
- The IDE passes a protected marker and the project path, and the CLI drops empty, '.', relative and in-project PATH entries and sets NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath before it resolves claude.
- Or the IDE passes an absolute, validated MOE_CLAUDE_BIN.

Cover JetBrains (TerminalAgentLauncher.kt, after task-26d9dc26) and VS Code (after its twin row). Legacy behaviour stays unchanged.
definitionOfDone: Under the protected profile, an accounts CLI started from either IDE never runs a claude or node reached through the project cwd or an empty, '.', relative or in-project PATH entry, and it refuses with a clear message when no such claude exists outside the project.
Legacy accounts CLI behaviour and Accounts lines are unchanged, and tests cover the Windows lookup (PATHEXT, the cmd shim) and the POSIX lookup.

(1) ClaudeCommand gains `pinned?: { path: string; cwd: string; cmd?: string }`: the claude child's PATH, its working directory and, on Windows for a .cmd or .bat claude, the absolute cmd.exe. Export `class ProtectedClaudeRefused extends Error`.

(2) Export `protectedClaudeCommand(env, project): ClaudeCommand`, on the host platform only. Two rules first:
- Local: on win32 a path is usable only if it is drive-qualified (a letter, a colon, then a slash or backslash). UNC, device, rooted and drive-relative forms are not. Elsewhere it must be absolute. Its fs.realpathSync.native must succeed and, on win32, still be drive-qualified, because a mapped drive resolves to UNC.
- In project: walk the real path and each path.dirname ancestor. It is in the project when an ancestor equals the project's real path (lower-cased on win32 and darwin), or has the project's bigint stat identity (dev and ino, with ino not 0n). This is the -ef walk of protected_trusted_dir in scripts/moe-agent.sh. On drvfs, realpath keeps a case-variant spelling, but the identity matches. A failed stat counts as in the project.

Then, in this order, throwing ProtectedClaudeRefused with these exact reasons:
- project: local and a directory, else 'the project <arg> is not a local folder'.
- PATH: env.PATH exactly on POSIX; envValue(env, 'PATH') on win32, trimmed and with surrounding double quotes stripped, as findWindowsCommand does. Split it by path.delimiter. Keep each local directory that is not in the project, as its real path, in order, once. If none is kept: 'no absolute PATH entry is outside the project <arg>'.
- cwd: env.HOME on POSIX, envValue(env, 'USERPROFILE') on win32, else os.homedir(). It must be local, a directory and not in the project, else 'the home folder <home> is not a local folder outside the project <arg>'.
- claude: bin = MOE_CLAUDE_BIN trimmed, or 'claude'.
  - A bin holding a path separator must be a local regular file not in the project, else 'MOE_CLAUDE_BIN <bin> is not an absolute file outside the project <arg>'.
  - A bare bin is searched in the kept entries, in order. On win32 use the PATHEXT names findWindowsCommand builds: extract that one rule into a helper both use, so findWindowsCommand behaves exactly as before. On POSIX use the bare name.
  - Accept the first candidate whose real path is a regular file not in the project and, on POSIX, passes fs.accessSync(real, X_OK). If none: MOE_PROTECTED_CLAUDE_NOT_FOUND.
- Result:
  - A .js/.mjs/.cjs real file runs as {file: process.execPath, prefix: [real]}.
  - A win32 .exe or .com, and any POSIX file, runs as {file: real, shell: false}.
  - Any other win32 file needs the shell. cmd must be a local regular file not in the project at path.win32.join(SystemRoot from envValue, 'System32', 'cmd.exe'), else 'cmd.exe under SystemRoot <value, or (unset)> is not a local file outside the project <arg>'.
  - pinned = {path: kept.join(path.delimiter), cwd, cmd when set}; missing is false.

Messages, exactly:
- 'MOE_PROTECTED_CLAUDE_REFUSED: <reason>; nothing was run.'
- 'MOE_PROTECTED_CLAUDE_NOT_FOUND: "<bin>" was not found on an absolute PATH entry outside the project <arg>; nothing was run. Install Claude Code outside the project and put its folder on PATH, then try again.'

(2) Export `protectedClaudeCommand(env, project): ClaudeCommand`, on the host platform only. Two rules first:
- Local: on win32 a path is usable only if it is drive-qualified (a letter, a colon, then a slash or backslash). UNC, device, rooted and drive-relative forms are not. Elsewhere it must be absolute. Its fs.realpathSync.native must succeed and, on win32, still be drive-qualified, because a mapped drive resolves to UNC.
- In project: walk the real path and each path.dirname ancestor. It is in the project when an ancestor equals the project's real path (lower-cased on win32 and darwin), or has the project's bigint stat identity (dev and ino, with ino not 0n). - project: local and a directory, else 'the project <arg> is not a local folder'.
- PATH: env.PATH exactly on POSIX; envValue(env, 'PATH') on win32, trimmed and with surrounding double quotes stripped, as findWindowsCommand does. Split it by path.delimiter.
